subject: Proposed City Charter Ballot Question Information Campaign
overview: The Council approved a five-year library digitization contract and a historic preservation grant for the Unitarian Universalist Church. Members also requested a city-wide information campaign regarding the upcoming charter reform ballot question and tabled the Mayor's amended investment ordinance.

items.title: Meeting Minutes and Committee Reports
items.summary: The Council approved the records of the October 7, 2025 meeting and reports from the Public Health and Community Safety Committee regarding local health services and ICE enforcement impacts.

items.title: Values Aligned Local Investments Ordinance
items.summary: The Council tabled the amended investment ordinance until the next regular meeting to allow for further review.

items.title: Library Digitization Contract Approval
items.summary: Approved a five-year contract with AM Quartex, funded by a Bloomberg Digital Innovation Grant, to host and maintain a digital repository for the library's local history collections.

items.title: Bicycle Advisory Commission Donation Acceptance
items.summary: Approved a $500 donation from Beacon Bank for bicycle safety equipment, amended to ensure the funds are deposited into the commission's specific account rather than the general fund.

items.title: Unitarian Universalist Church Historic Window Preservation
items.summary: Approved $9,000 in Community Preservation Act funds for the East Window Preservation Project at the Unitarian Universalist Church of Medford.

items.title: City Charter Ballot Question Public Information
items.summary: Passed a resolution requesting the Mayor utilize robocalls and the city website to inform voters about the proposed city charter and where to find its full text before the November 4th election.

items.title: DPW Accident Claim Settlement
items.summary: Approved a $3,000 settlement with Safety Insurance Company for a property damage claim involving a Department of Public Works vehicle.

items.title: Public Participation
items.summary: Residents spoke on topics including I-93 sound barriers, the legality of the proposed values-aligned investment ordinance, and the necessity of geographic representation through charter reform.
